thread:
Asha: Heads-up: NebulaCloud reached out asking for Redwood reference arch + Terraform registry modules for their marketplace listing. They want support for AWS and Azure in the initial beta. Can we scope?

Ethan: Important to define what "support" means. Do they want identical modules for both clouds or a common interface with cloud-specific implementations?

Leila: Recommend a common interface (inputs/outputs) with provider-specific modules under modules/aws and modules/azure. Consumers call the root module which proxies to the proper provider module via `count`/`for_each`. Simplifies docs and registry UX.

Joon: Agree. Also add a small `examples/` folder per cloud showing VPC/NSG, instance pool, and how to wire up private control plane registration. Keep examples minimal for marketplace listing.

Asha: Nebula insisted on: Terraform Registry entry, semantic versioning, changelog, and a GitHub Actions publish flow that tags + publishes to registry on release. Can we include that?

Ethan: Yes. GH Actions will need a Terraform Registry API token stored in org secrets. We should include a dry-run workflow that validates the `registry` manifest and runs `terraform init` for each module.

Leila: CI plan: matrix for terraform fmt, validate, `terraform init -backend=false`, and `terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan`. For integration smoke tests we can run in a partner sandbox account with short-lived creds. CI-bot: we need to ensure secrets rotation and least privilege.

CI-bot: Note: sandbox provisioning will require ephemeral credentials via OIDC to avoid long-lived keys. Recommend `deploy-role` with limited scope for test deploys.

Joon: For marketplace listing, Nebula wants a bundled AMI/image for fast deploy. We should avoid shipping models baked into images for export control reasons. Recommend images that pull model artifacts at runtime from Redwood-hosted registry or partner-controlled S3. Document both approaches.

Asha: Good call. Also they asked for terraform variables for billing tags and marketplace product id. Make sure module supports `tags` map and `marketplace_product_id` input.

Leila: Security inputs to include: `kms_key_arn`, `enable_private_network_endpoint` (bool), `allowed_cidrs`, and `control_plane_registration_token` (sensitive). Document how to rotate that token.

Ethan: On Azure specifics: include support for Accelerated Networking VM sizes, Managed Disks encrypted with customer-managed keys, and an optional AKS path for node pools with GPU-enabled SKU.

Joon: Outputs should include: endpoint_url, instance_count, resource_ids, and `module_version`. Also provide a `metadata.json` for registry that includes supported regions/regions matrix.

Asha: Nebula's product team wants an automated cost-estimate card as part of the listing. We can include a `cost_estimate.md` script that uses instance hourly rates + egress estimate. Keep as guidance, not SLA.

CI-bot: Perf test suggestion: add a lightweight harness that deploys minimal cluster and runs a 1-minute load generator hitting health and tokenized generation endpoint. This runs nightly in partner sandbox.

Leila: License question: Nebula requires examples to be MIT, modules can be Apache-2.0. Confirm legal. We'll add a `LICENSES.md` in repo describing each folder license.

Ethan: Docs: top-level quickstart, provider-specific walkthroughs, troubleshooting (common errors: AMI mismatch, subnet conflicts, DNS issues), and onboarding checklist for Nebula ops (webhook URL, expected inbound traffic, support contact).

Joon: Add a `provisioning-hooks/` folder with cloud-init scripts and an `onboard.sh` sample that calls `https://partners.nebulacloud.example/onboard` with instance metadata. Make it opt-in.

Asha: Timeline: Nebula asked for a partner-ready draft in 4 weeks. Can we hit that?

Leila: 4 weeks doable if we scope MVP: root module + aws module + azure skeleton + examples for both + GH Actions + basic docs. Leave extended tests and AKS path for follow-up.

Ethan: Owners: modules & CI -> Ethan & Joon, docs & examples -> Leila, partner packaging & registry manifest -> Asha. Due dates: modules CI initial -> in 12 days; docs/examples -> in 14 days; registry manifest -> in 18 days.

Asha: I'll prepare a partner checklist for Nebula including legal review, export control note, and marketplace screenshots. Will add to repo `PARTNER_CHECKLIST.md`.

Leila: Small UX note: ensure root module exposes a `deployment_type` var (values: vm | k8s) so Nebula can show both options in their marketplace UI.

Joon: For the Terraform Registry, we must ensure module naming uses `redwoodio` namespace and `redwood-private-nebula-shim` slug to avoid collisions. Also pin provider versions in `required_providers` to avoid surprises.

CI-bot: Action item created: `nebula-module-beta` - tasks: scaffold repo, aws module, azure module skeleton, examples, README, CI. Assigned: Asha, Ethan, Leila, Joon.

Ethan: One more constraint from infra: Nebula wants automated backups of any local model cache to partner S3. We'll add optional `cache_backup` block with `enabled`, `bucket_arn`, `retention_days`.

Asha: Great. I'll set up the GitHub repo and invite Nebula's engineers as collaborators for early feedback. Scheduling follow-up sync next Wednesday. If anyone hits a blocker, flag here. :thumbsup:
